Formulation  
Patient, a 32-year-old male medical doctor with a family history of stroke, presents with evolving transient neurological symptoms (right hand numbness/pins and needles, right arm and leg weakness, gait abnormalities) increasing in frequency over 1.5–2 months. Episodes last a few days, currently associated with impaired hand function. No visual, speech, swallowing difficulties or persistent neurological symptoms outside episodes. Fatigue and low energy are additional symptoms. The symptoms raise concern for transient ischemic attacks given family history and symptom pattern. Protective factors include good insight, stable living situation, and access to healthcare. The urgency of investigation and referral stems from potential stroke risk. No mental health diagnosis at present.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem (Suspected TIAs / transient neurological symptoms):  
- Patient Goal(s): To receive timely assessment and diagnosis to clarify cause of symptoms and reduce risk of stroke  
- Clinical Goal(s): Expedite referral and assessment at TIA/stroke clinic; exclude cerebrovascular pathology; initiate appropriate management if indicated  
- Actions (Patient): Attend TIA clinic appointment urgently; monitor symptoms; seek emergency care if symptoms persist or worsen (e.g., prolonged weakness)  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Refer urgently to TIA clinic with appropriate clinical information; provide patient with contact details for TIA clinic and advice on when to seek emergency care; support patient communication with hospital services  

Secondary Problem (Fatigue and low energy):  
- Patient Goal(s): To understand cause and management of fatigue  
- Clinical Goal(s): Monitor for fatigue and associated symptoms; consider further evaluation once neurological diagnosis clarified  
- Actions (Patient): Report any worsening symptoms or new symptoms  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Review fatigue symptoms post-assessment; consider supportive interventions or investigations if symptoms persist  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics covered include recognition of TIA symptoms, importance of urgent assessment, when to seek emergency care, follow-up procedures  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Prolonged or persistent neurological symptoms, difficulty swallowing, speech changes, vision changes, gait disturbance lasting longer than typical episodes  
- Coping Strategies: Not recorded
